today.title: Heat-day check-ins for elderly and ill residents

effect.text: Lowers your exposure, not the temperature
effect.note: Reduces health risk; does not lower the temperature

steps: Make a volunteer list in the RWA group
Start check-ins when Thandak shows High or above

quick.title: Drinking-water points

because.text: Part of every home's daily plan

effect.text: Health measure recommended by NCDC (no temperature claim)

steps: Put out drinking water (and ORS) at busy spots, parks, bus stops and markets.
Put them near gates, markets and bus stops, where vendors, guards and delivery workers stop

sources.title: NCDC heat-wave advisory for state health departments (2026)

quick.title: Cool room / cooling shelter

because.text: Part of every home's daily plan

effect.text: Health measure recommended by NCDC (no temperature claim)

steps: During heat alerts, set up an airy or cooled room with water and ORS for older people, children and anyone unwell.
Use schools, community halls and health centres you already have; the ward ranking shows where to start

sources.title: NCDC heat-wave advisory for state health departments (2026)

moderate.title: Colony-wide cool-roof painting drive

because.text: A common fix (no local satellite data here yet)

effect.note: Per home. Roofs, light paving and shade trees together cool the whole area most
effect.status: Verified (Vellingiri 2020 full text; Arumugam 2013 from conference abstract page only; older than 5 y; small samples)

steps: Count the dark roofs in the colony
Buy the coating in bulk through the RWA for a lower price
Start with top-floor homes and homes with elderly residents

sources.title: Vellingiri et al. 2020, Indian J Occup Environ Med (16 Ahmedabad slum homes, roof comparison)
Telangana Announces a Groundbreaking Cool Roof Policy (NRDC)
Arumugam R et al. 2013 Proc. 34th AIVC/2nd Cool Roofs Conf. Athens; Vellingiri S et al. Indian J Occup Environ Med 2020;24(1):25-29

moderate.title: Shade sails or pergolas over lanes, parks and waiting spots

because.text: A common fix (no local satellite data here yet)

steps: Shade the most-used walking routes and bus stops first
Use light-coloured, breathable fabric so hot air can escape

long.title: Plant dense native shade trees

because.text: A common fix (no local satellite data here yet)

effect.text: Range comes from a global review, not a promise for your area
effect.note: Dense native trees cool streets most in dry climates, but can keep nights slightly warmer

steps: Prefer native species such as neem and arjuna over ornamental trees
Plant on bare ground and along south/west edges of streets

sources.title: Wrong trees in the wrong place can make cities hotter at night (University of Cambridge)
Cooling cities needs climate-smart design, not just more trees (Mongabay India, on IIT Gandhinagar / Northeastern study of 138 Indian cities)

long.title: Light-coloured or permeable paving for open areas

because.text: A common fix (no local satellite data here yet)

steps: Replace dark asphalt in parking and courtyards when it is due for repair
Use grass pavers where cars park rarely

long.title: Revive ponds and add rainwater harvesting

because.text: A common fix (no local satellite data here yet)

steps: Find the dried ponds and water bodies nearby
Work with the municipality: this usually needs public land and budget

avoid.title: Don't use see-through roof sheets

because.text: Part of every home's daily plan

effect.text: Measured about 3 °C HOTTER than a tin roof (Ahmedabad)

steps: Don't put up translucent or skylight roof sheets (such as Airlite) to cool a room.

sources.title: Vellingiri et al. 2020, Indian J Occup Environ Med (16 Ahmedabad slum homes, roof comparison)

excluded.title: Plant spaced-out trees that keep air moving

reason.text: Not suited to your area's climate

sources.title: Arumugam R et al. 2013 Proc. 34th AIVC/2nd Cool Roofs Conf. Athens; Vellingiri S et al. Indian J Occup Environ Med 2020;24(1):25-29
sources.status: Verified (Vellingiri 2020 full text; Arumugam 2013 from conference abstract page only; older than 5 y; small samples)
